definitions.gloss: to bump into; to run into unexpectedly; to encounter by chance
definitions.explanation: To unexpectedly come face to face with someone, often in an awkward or unwanted situation. Can also refer to things colliding.

examples.japanese: {元|もと}カノと{鉢合|はちあ}わせた。
{廊下|ろうか}で{社長|しゃちょう}と{鉢合|はちあ}わせてしまった。
examples.english: I accidentally bumped into the company president in the hallway.

examples.japanese: {泥棒|どろぼう}が{家|いえ}の{中|なか}で{住人|じゅうにん}と{鉢合|はちあ}わせて{逃|に}げた。
examples.english: The burglar ran into the resident inside the house and fled.

notes:
USAGE:
Literally refers to pots ({鉢|はち}) bumping together. Usually implies the encounter is unexpected and often unwanted or awkward. The noun form {鉢合|はちあ}わせ is also common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- 〜と{鉢合|はちあ}わせる (to bump into someone)
- {鉢合|はちあ}わせになる (to end up running into each other)
- {偶然|ぐうぜん}{鉢合|はちあ}わせる (to encounter by coincidence)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {出|で}くわす: to come across, to run into — similar meaning but slightly more casual
- {遭遇|そうぐう}する: to encounter — more formal, used for both people and situations
